what: Information is carried by colour alone in several places. (1) In speed drills, the correct answer is shown only by a green outline and the chosen wrong one by a red outline, and the feedback text does not name the right answer. (2) The interpreter step badges show ok/warn/bad only by background colour. (3) In sims, abnormal vitals have only a red border and red number, and done actions only a green border. (4) Session and round progress squares are green or red only. (5) The severity bar is a gradient only. Users with red-green colour blindness cannot tell right from wrong, and screen readers get nothing. Fails WCAG 1.4.1.
evidence: Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-speed-answered.png (two outlined options, identical apart from hue). Screenshots /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-interp-steps-dark.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-ans-sim-light.png.
fix: Speed: prefix the label with ✓ or ✗ (as .opt kbd does in sessions), add aria-label suffixes " — correct answer" and " — your answer", and print "Answer: <label>" in spFb. Steps: put ✓ ! ✗ inside the badge (keep the number in an sr-only span), or add "ok/check/problem" text. Vitals: add a ▲/▼ marker or the word "high/low" and a visually hidden "abnormal". Done actions: add a "✓ done" text suffix. Progress squares: give the container aria-label "3 of 10 right", plus a pattern (hatched for missed).

what: Light theme (both skins; clinical reuses the same colours) fails WCAG AA 4.5:1 for small text in many places. --accent-ink #B9480A on --accent-soft #FBDFC8 is 4.13 (active tab label at 9px, streak chip, .numk, chips, "Older adults →") and on --bg is 4.44 (every eyebrow). --muted #75685A on --surface-2 #EDE3D0 is 4.25 (156 instances: small labels, inactive seg buttons such as "Venous", .teachbar, Henderson step text) and on --surface-3 is 3.84. --good #2E7D4F is 4.26 on bg and 3.96 on surface-2 (the ✓ kbd). --warn #A86A00 is 3.63 on warn-soft (the "Hint" label). White on --warn step badges is 4.44. Dark theme passes except --null.
evidence: Computed from the tokens, and confirmed by a per-element scan of all 60 views in light pixel and light clinical (aud-light-*.json). Ratios: accent-ink/accent-soft 4.13, muted/surface-2 4.25, muted/surface-3 3.84, good/surface-2 3.96, warn/warn-soft 3.63.
fix: Light tokens: --accent-ink:#9E3D06 (5.28 on accent-soft, 5.68 on bg); --muted:#64584B (5.43 on surface-2, 4.9 on surface-3); --good:#256B42 (5.06 on surface-2); --warn:#7F4F00 (≥5 on warn-soft). Keep --accent for fills only, never for text in light.

where: .stepl li.ok>i, .stepl li.warn>i, .stepl li.bad>i (and .qn on answered session questions)
what: Dark theme: white step numbers on --good #84CC16 (1.98:1), --warn #E3B860 (1.86:1) and --bad #FF5F4F (3.0:1) are unreadable. The ✓ in .qn on --good is 1.98.
evidence: Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-interp-steps-dark.png (the badges "1" and "2"). Contrast scan: "#ffffff on #84cc16 11px 1.98", "#ffffff on #e3b860 11px 1.86".
fix: Use color:var(--on-accent) (#0B0907) on these badges in dark (10.1, 10.7 and 6.6:1), and keep #fff only in light, where the fills are dark. Simplest fix: color:var(--bg) in dark and var(--raise) in light, or define --on-good/--on-warn/--on-bad tokens.

where: Sticky header.top, fixed nav.tabs, fixed #roundbar, sticky .sbar: no scroll-padding
what: Keyboard focus is often completely hidden under the sticky header or the fixed bottom tab bar or round bar (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured). At 200% zoom on desktop (640×400 CSS px) during a Round, the header (62) + session bar (60) + round bar (62) cover 46% of the viewport.
evidence: obsc.py, phone 390×844, lesson hh: Tab lands on option C at y=795–844, 49/49 px under the bottom nav; Shift+Tab lands on option B at y=0–49, under the header. At 640×400 in a Round, option 3 is 62/66 px under #roundbar. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-z200-roundsess.png.
fix: html{scroll-padding-top:calc(var(--hdr-h,72px) + 8px);scroll-padding-bottom:calc(var(--nav-h,72px) + 8px)}, plus an extra 70px of bottom padding when body.inround, and 60px of top padding for .sbar in session. Optionally make the header non-sticky when the viewport height is under 500px.

what: touch-action:none on .sheet blocks finger scrolling inside every sheet. When a sheet is taller than 86vh (the OCR confirm sheet with 13 fields, the Round builder with 6 or more legs, or any sheet at large text sizes or 200% zoom), the top of the sheet cannot be reached by touch. In the OCR sheet that top part holds the heading, the privacy note, the Arterial/Venous toggle and the pH field.
evidence: touch.py (has_touch, 390×560): ocrSheet open, scrollHeight 845 > clientHeight 480; a CDP touch swipe gives scrollTop 0. With touch-action set to pan-y, the same swipe gives scrollTop 365.
fix: Change it to .sheet{touch-action:pan-y}. Keep the swipe-down-to-close only on .sheet-grab, or only when sheet.scrollTop===0.

where: .ctrl input, .fld input, .inp, select.tool, .seg, input[type=range] track: border var(--line)
what: Form controls are outlined with --line, which is 1.42–1.78:1 against the light backgrounds and 1.4–1.61:1 in dark. WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1 for component boundaries. Inputs are hard to find, especially the empty OCR and gas-log fields. The light-theme focus indicator (accent #F26A1B outline on #F3EBDD) is 2.59:1, also below 3:1. The input focus style removes the outline and only recolours the border to the same accent.
evidence: Token maths: line/bg light 1.53, line/surface 1.68, line/surface-2 1.42; dark line/bg 1.61. accent/bg light 2.59. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-savesheet.png (faint field borders).
fix: Add --field-line: light #8F8270 (3.48 on surface), dark #756859 (3.67 on bg), and use it for input, select, textarea and range borders. Focus ring in light: outline-color #C2560F (3.83) or #B9480A, with a 2px inner --bg ring. For inputs keep an outline (do not set outline:none) or add box-shadow:0 0 0 3px var(--accent-ink).

what: Dark theme: the round bar is drawn in --ink (#F3EDE6, light) with the "Round · leg 1/3" eyebrow in --accent #F97316, which is 2.41:1 at 10px.
fix: Use .rb-in .eyebrow{color:var(--deep)} (#9A3412, 6.29:1 on #F3EDE6). Or, since the bar inverts per theme, define --rb-accent: light theme #F26A1B on dark ink, dark theme #9A3412.

what: Headings skip levels, and several views have no h1. Sessions (all 11 modes) have no h1: steps, today, quick, due, gotd and boss have only question h3s, and fit, reflex, gym, mist and final have no headings at all. Speed drills have no headings. Chat, image and sim cases start at h2. Learn, models, tools and Settings go h1 → h3. Progress goes h1 → h4. Sim goes h2 → h4. Section labels such as "Bedside tools" and "Models" (Labs), "Today's plan", "Gas of the day", "Hook" (Today), "Last 4 weeks", "Calibration", "Training numbers" (Progress), "Look", "Reading gases", "Practice" (Settings), and "Results" and "Events" (sim) are styled eyebrow spans, not headings. Heading navigation, the main way screen-reader users skim, misses most of the page.
evidence: Heading lists from audit.js per view (aud-dark-pixel-390.json) and aria snapshots snap-*.txt.
fix: Give each view exactly one h1 (the session title in .sbar, the speed drill name, the case title), make section labels h2, and make sub-items h3. Fix this mainly in the render functions of ui1, ui2, ui3, ui5, ui7 and ui8. Keep the visual style by putting class="eyebrow" on the heading.

where: 44 px targets (.crumbs button, .seg button, .tool, input[type=range], .ctrl input, select.tool, summary, .linkbtn, .gl .de, .rb-in .btn)
what: The CSS comment "4.1: 44px touch targets" is not met in many places. At 390 px: crumb back buttons ("← Labs", "← Learn", "← Practice", "← Cases") are 24 px high. Segmented buttons are 29 px (Practice difficulty; gases-per-session "5" is 30×29; Settings Look and Theme; Arterial/Venous; case and glossary filters; Sure/Think/Guess). Model preset .tool buttons are 29–31 px. Range sliders are 30 px. Number inputs are 40 px. #iLoad is 34 px. <summary> ("Sources · 2", "What the reader saw") is 24 px. "Older adults →" is 24 px. Glossary terms are 32 px. Round bar: Go is 43 px wide and ✕ is 36 px wide. All of these pass WCAG 2.2 AA (24 px) but miss the app's own 44 px standard for on-shift phone use.
fix: Add min-height:44px to .crumbs button, .seg button, .tool, summary, .linkbtn, .gl .de and input[type=range]; add min-height:44px to the inputs and selects in .ctrl and .fld; add min-width:44px to .rb-in .btn; give the crumbs a padding:10px 4px hit area.

where: Reflow at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10; 1280 px at 400%)
what: The gas slip table and the noisy printout overflow the page width at 320 px: the document is 356–374 px wide in sessions, Today's gas of the day, reflex, final and the Real printouts drill. That forces horizontal page scrolling and pushes the reference-range column off-screen. 640×400 (200% zoom of 1280×800) reflows correctly.
evidence: reflow.py 320×568: today docW 356; sess-gotd 374; speed-noisy 356 (.printout and .spo buttons R=356). Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-reflow320-sess-steps.png.
fix: At max-width:360px, hide the .slip reference-range column (as .printout .rr is already hidden at ≤520px), allow wrapping (white-space:normal) in .slip td, and put .slip and .printout inside overflow-x:auto wrappers.

what: The clinical skin swaps the pixel font for Atkinson but keeps the 9–10 px sizes (290 text runs at 9 px and 270 at 10 px across the views). Atkinson at 9 px is much smaller on screen than the pixel font, so the "calmer" skin is the harder one to read. All sizes are in px, so a user's browser default font size (text-only scaling) has no effect.
fix: In the clinical skin, set a 12 px minimum for .eyebrow, small, .chip, nav.tabs button, .seg button, kbd and .mt small: html[data-skin=clinical] .eyebrow,…{font-size:max(12px,.75rem)}. Over time, move body text and labels to rem.

where: Missing skip link; tab order of the bottom nav
what: There is no "Skip to content" link. On every view, the keyboard passes 7 header stops (brand, 5 tabs, gear) before the content. On phone widths the tab bar sits visually at the bottom but comes first in DOM and focus order.
evidence: kb.py: the Tab sequence from load is brand, Today, Learn, Labs, Practice, Progress, Settings, then #tRound.
fix: Add <a class="skip" href="#main"> as the first child of body (visible on focus). Give <main> tabindex=-1. This combines with the focus-on-h1 fix in go().

where: No <meta charset> and no <html lang> in shell.html (artifact build)
what: buffer.html and the frozen test copy start with <title>, with no charset and no lang. Opened as a file (and in any host that does not add a skeleton), Chromium sometimes guesses the wrong encoding. One of my test runs at 320 px rendered "ðŸ”¥ 0", "PvCOâ‚‚" and "7.35â€“7.45" throughout. Without lang, screen readers may pick the wrong voice. The PWA index.html is correct (lang="en", meta charset utf-8). Doubt: the claude.ai artifact wrapper may add both.
evidence: reflow.py 320×568 screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T27-reflow320-sess-steps.png (mojibake), while the same file rendered correctly in other runs.
fix: Start shell.html with <meta charset="utf-8"> (it is harmless inside the artifact wrapper). If the wrapper does not add lang, set document.documentElement.lang="en-GB" in boot().

what: The app has rich shortcuts (1–7, H, Enter, Esc, arrows in flash cards), but they are discoverable only by reading kbd hints.
fix: Press "?" to open a modal listing the shortcuts for the current view, using the shared modal helper.
